ed70939f.task:
You are the validation AND reporting agent for the admin authorization weaknesses in /workspace/Loja-Online (React/Vite SPA + Supabase). Validate each issue with concrete evidence (static trace + local dynamic validation only), then file vulnerability report(s) with the fix inlined (code_locations fix_before/fix_after + fix_pr_body). DO NOT send any requests to the hosted Supabase project (qnkqcljhvnburzbyxwks.supabase.co) — it is out of scope; all validation must be local (code tracing, local build/bundle inspection, node_modules API source).

Issues to validate:
A) Publicly-discoverable admin registration secret: `.env` (tracked in git) has VITE_ADMIN_SECRET_KEY=minha_chave_secreta_vitta. `src/services/authService.ts` signUp() grants role='admin' in supabase user_metadata whenever this secret matches. Since it is a VITE_* variable it is inlined into the production JS bundle for every visitor. Prove locally: run `npm run build` (or `npx vite build`) and grep the dist bundle for `minha_chave_secreta_vitta` / `VITE_ADMIN_SECRET_KEY` / the env value. Map the full chain: any visitor extracts secret -> AdminSignUpPage (src/components/pages/AdminSignUpPage.tsx) -> authService.signUp -> user_metadata.role=admin -> RLS policies in supabase/migrations/20260815231300_schema.sql grant INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on products/categories and UPDATE on orders to auth.jwt() user_metadata role=admin.
B) Client-controlled role in user_metadata (bypasses the secret entirely): signup stores role in user_metadata; Supabase allows any authenticated user to update their own user_metadata via supabase.auth.updateUser({data:{role:'admin'}}) (verify the API exists in node_modules/@supabase/ supabase-js or @supabase/auth-js source); the RLS policies then trust auth.jwt()->'user_metadata'->>'role'='admin'. This is a complete privilege escalation with no secret. Also confirm the app's frontend gate is `isAdmin = state.user?.role === 'admin'` in src/context/AuthContext.tsx and App.tsx renders TomatoAdminPanel purely on that client-side check.
C) Default admin credentials: src/components/pages/AdminLoginPage.tsx pre-fills admin@vittabasics.com / admin123 and displays "Demo: admin@vittabasics.com / admin123".

Decide reporting granularity. Likely: one Critical/High report for the admin privilege escalation (A+B chained — same root cause: role controlled by client and trusted by RLS), and optionally a Low/Info for the demo default credentials if you deem it separate. For A+B the fix: never derive privileges from client-supplied user_metadata; introduce a server-side role store (e.g., profiles table with role column, set via a secure trigger or security-definer function; RLS checks profiles.role = 'admin' using auth.uid()), and replace the client-string-compare secret with server-side verification (e.g., RPC function that validates the secret server-side and sets the role in the profiles table). Provide concrete fix_before/fix_after for src/services/authService.ts (and mention the migration SQL changes in fix_pr_body / remediation). Use CWE-269 or CWE-287 as appropriate (check exact IDs), and derive honest CVSS metrics from the demonstrated chain (escalation to admin CRUD on products/categories/orders). Use create_vulnerability_report with full fields.

Use exec_command with login=false, tty=true. Finish with agent_finish summarizing what you validated and filed.

78120187.task:
You are the validation AND reporting agent for access-control weaknesses in /workspace/Loja-Online (React/Vite SPA + Supabase). Validate with concrete evidence (static analysis of SQL + code; local validation only — do NOT make requests to the hosted Supabase project qnkqcljhvnburzbyxwks.supabase.co, it is out of scope) and file vulnerability report(s) with fixes inlined (code_locations + fix_pr_body).

Focus areas:
1. Supabase RLS review: supabase/migrations/20260815231300_schema.sql. Assess every policy:
   - products/categories: SELECT public; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE gated only on auth.jwt() user_metadata role=admin (client-controlled claim — cross-reference this flaw; your finding should complement, not duplicate, the admin-escalation report).
   - orders: INSERT policy checks auth.uid() = user_id — but user_id is provided by the CLIENT in the insert payload (src/services/tomatoApi.ts createOrder sets user_id: sessionData.session.user.id, which is fine, but does the policy stop a client from inserting an order for a DIFFERENT user_id? auth.uid() = user_id compares to the request's authenticated uid — verify: if the client sends another user's UUID as user_id, the policy auth.uid()=user_id fails, so no cross-user insert — confirm this reasoning in your report).
   - orders: SELECT policy `auth.uid() = user_id OR role=admin`. Check getOrders() in tomatoApi.ts: if requested by a logged-in user without a valid session supabase silently returns RLS-filtered rows; the fallback localStorage path in getOrders returns INITIAL_ORDERS to ANY user — assess whether that leaks demo customer PII (names/emails/addresses) to unauthenticated visitors (it is static demo data — classify honestly).
   - order_items: INSERT policy uses `order_id IN (SELECT id FROM public.orders WHERE user_id = auth.uid())` — evaluate whether an attacker can insert items into own orders only; also whether order_items has UPDATE/DELETE policies missing.
   - updateOrderStatus() in tomatoApi.ts updates orders.status with NO server-side role check in code (relies entirely on RLS) — confirm the only enforcement point is the flawed user_metadata role policy.
2. Client-side-only admin gating: App.tsx renders TomatoAdminPanel only when `isAuthenticated && isAdmin` (client state). mapSupabaseUser reads role from user_metadata. Confirm no other enforcement exists.
3. IDOR checks: getProductById(id) (any id readable — public anyway), getOrders (RLS-scoped), updateOrderStatus(orderId) — does the code allow a customer to change their own order status? (RLS: UPDATE allowed only for admin role). Any other object-level access issue?
4. Search filter: getProducts uses query.or(`name.ilike.%${search}%,description.ilike.%${search}%`) with raw interpolation into a PostgREST filter string — assess (not SQLi due to parameterization, but note any PostgREST-specific risk like wildcard abuse/DoS) and mention only if genuinely relevant.

Report ONLY what is a real, demonstrable weakness with concrete impact. Likely candidates: missing RLS policy for orders UPDATE by customers is actually a control (good); the real systemic issue is the user_metadata role trust (covered elsewhere — do NOT duplicate; reference it in remediation context). If you find a distinct access-control issue (e.g., missing RLS UPDATE/DELETE policy on order_items leaving admin-only by default = secure; runaway: no DELETE policy on orders at all; localStorage fallback leaking demo order data to unauthenticated users), file it as its own report with fix. CVSS must map to demonstrated impact. Use create_vulnerability_report (never create_dependency_report). If you conclude no distinct valid finding beyond the escalation issue, say so explicitly in agent_finish — do not file noise.

Use exec_command with login=false, tty=true. Finish with agent_finish summarizing validated findings and reports filed.

32339d04.task:
You are the validation AND reporting agent for e-commerce business-logic weaknesses in /workspace/Loja-Online (React/Vite SPA + Supabase). Validate with concrete evidence (static code tracing; local validation only — do NOT send requests to hosted Supabase qnkqcljhvnburzbyxwks.supabase.co) and file vulnerability report(s) with fixes inlined (code_locations + fix_pr_body).

Focus areas:
1. Client-controlled order totals/prices: src/services/tomatoApi.ts createOrder() inserts `totalAmount: orderPayload.totalAmount || 0` and order_items with `price`/`quantity` taken verbatim from the client payload. Only RLS check on INSERT is auth.uid()=user_id. Trace the call site (CartContext.tsx checkout flow / CartDrawer.tsx) to confirm the total and item prices originate in client state, so an authenticated user can submit an order with totalAmount 0 / arbitrary values or negative/goofy quantities. Confirm whether any server-side recomputation exists (none in this codebase). Pivot: create an order with negative amount, zero amount, or tampered item prices — what integrity impact on the store's orders data? Note: no payment gateway integration found — assess impact honestly (order records integrity / downstream manual fulfillment). Also check stockCount decrement logic (if any).
2. Coupon abuse: src/services/tomatoApi.ts getCoupons/applyCoupon/saveCoupon/deleteCoupon operate ONLY on localStorage (client-side). Anyone can add arbitrary coupon codes server-less; discounts are computed client-side. Trace where applyCoupon is used (CartContext / CartDrawer) to confirm discount math is client-side and coupons never validated server-side.
3. Cart manipulation: src/context/CartContext.tsx — negative quantities, price fields from INITIAL_PRODUCTS vs local product data (products editable in localStorage via saveProduct fallback), cart totals, race conditions on rapid add/remove (low signal — mention only if genuinely demonstrable).
4. Signup/account flow oddities in ClientSignUpPage.tsx (e.g., role tampering in UI, admin secret accepted on client signup page?) — check.

Report only real weaknesses with demonstrated impact; the strongest candidate is likely the client-controlled order amount/price integrity (business logic). For the fix: server-side computation/re-validation of totals (RPC function / trigger recomputing totalAmount from order_items and product prices; CHECK constraints totalAmount >= 0, quantity >= 1), server-side coupon table with validation, reject unknown fields. Provide concrete code fix (e.g., migration SQL adding triggers/constraints, and changed createOrder to call an RPC). Use create_vulnerability_report with honest CVSS (this is an integrity-of-records issue; typically I:L, C:N or low C if order is addressed/fulfilled based on attacker data). Use CWE-840 or business-logic CWE if appropriate (verify ID).

Use exec_command with login=false, tty=true. Finish with agent_finish summarizing validated findings and reports filed.
